instruction: Library Link + Override `/home/user/Desktop/scene.blend` is an empty scene. `/home/user/Desktop/lib/characters.blend` is a library file containing a Collection named `Hero` with a single mesh object `HeroMesh` and a blue material `HeroMaterial`. Link that collection into the empty scene, create a local override of it, swap the override mesh to a new red local material, and save the result to `/home/user/Desktop/answer.blend`. ## Hard constraint: do not mutate the library file `/home/user/Desktop/lib/characters.blend` MUST remain byte-identical to its input state. Do not open it with `wm.open_mainfile`; do not save over it; do not pack or write into it. ## Requirements 1. `/home/user/Desktop/answer.blend` exists. 2. `/home/user/Desktop/lib/characters.blend` is byte-identical to its input SHA256 (recorded at `/home/user/Desktop/lib/characters.blend.sha256`). 3. A Collection named `Hero` exists in the saved file, is LOCAL (`library is None`), and is a library override (`override_library is not None`). 4. That collection contains a mesh object that is LOCAL and has `override_library` non-None. 5. The override mesh's material slot 0 holds a LOCAL material (not linked) that is NOT the original `HeroMaterial`, and whose Principled BSDF Base Color is red (R > 0.7, G < 0.3, B < 0.3). 6. Independently re-linking `HeroMaterial` from the library still yields the original blue Base Color (R < 0.3, G < 0.5, B > 0.6) - i.e. the lib material definition was not modified. Do not rename the `Hero` collection or the `HeroMesh` override object. [Software] Launch Blender by running `blender` from a terminal. For the steps below, use `/opt/blender/blender` for Blender command-line or background runs when working on `scene.blend`.
